subject: Veridian Health — EU-only inference and no-fallback request
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@veridianhealth.com>
To: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Veridian Health Procurement <procure@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: EU-only inference + no-fallback / forced model binding

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Veridian is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Before we proceed to procurement we need to confirm two hard requirements from our security & privacy teams that are non-negotiable for the pilot:

- EU-only inference residency: all inference must execute inside EU regions (data cannot leave the EU).
- No-fallback / forced model binding: under no circumstances can requests be routed to an alternative model or cross-region fallback. We must pin to a privacy-optimized variant (we asked for the privacy-int8 family during the demo).

Can Redwood support a contract-level clause and an operational guarantee for these? If not, please propose the minimal architecture (Dedicated / Private) and controls that will satisfy our auditors. Procurement is ready to proceed if we can get written confirmation + a simple mutual action plan.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement has a Q4 slot for pilots.

—Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Product Security
Veridian Health

Subject: Re: Request: EU-only inference + no-fallback / forced model binding

Markus / Hannah —

Reading Sara’s ask and based on our runtime constraints, here’s the pragmatic option set:

Option A (recommended): Dedicated EU-only pool (reserved capacity)
- Guarantees execution in EU region(s).
- We can bind service to a single model artifact (e.g., redwood-privacy-3b-int8) at the routing layer and disable automated fallback.
- Tradeoffs: reduced built-in redundancy; to preserve availability we'd provision burst capacity or a paired cluster in another EU AZ (not outside EU).
- Work required: provisioning lead time 2–4 weeks, infra config to hard-disable fallback routes, and a change to autoscaler policies.

Option B: Private (VPC) deployment inside customer cloud or VPC peering
- Strongest compliance posture; customer-controlled network.
- We can ship a preconfigured image with the specified model and no-fallback policy.
- Tradeoffs: longer lead time (4–8 weeks), integration work (KMS, IAM), and E2E runbook.

Operational caveat: disallowing any fallback increases risk of outages causing failed inference until capacity is available. For pilot we should define an availability SLO and an escalation path (hot standby or manual failover).

Deliverables I propose we attach to the MAP:
- Deployment topology (Dedicated EU-only)
- Model pinning confirmation (artifact hash + version)
- Audit controls: token-level logs, KV cache non-exfiltration checklist

I’ll prepare the infra checklist and the artifact hash for the variant. Hannah — anything from compliance side?

—Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: kms_integration_notes.md (draft), infra_provisioning_timeline.xlsx (internal)

Thanks Karthik — this aligns with Compliance. A few required controls before we sign off:

- VPC or Dedicated with Private networking in EU (no public egress to non-EU regions).
- CMK-backed encryption (customer-managed KMS) and proof of key residency.
- Audit logs retained 12 months (token-level usage redacted as per our policy) and accessible via our Console/Audit API.
- Signed attestation from Redwood that we will not change routing logic without 30 days’ notice and a technical rollback plan.

I’ve attached an EU residency checklist (eu_data_residency_checklist.xlsx) and a short attestation template. Legal will need to review the attestation and the MAP — looping them in after we send the proposed docs to Veridian.

Hannah Schmitt
Head, Security & Compliance

Sara — thanks for the patience. Based on our internal review we can meet Veridian’s requirements with a scoped Dedicated EU-only pilot and model binding. Summary below and next steps: 

Proposed pilot (2–4 weeks):
- Deployment: Dedicated GPU pool provisioned in our Frankfurt EU region.
- Model binding: pin to artifact redwood-privacy-3b-int8 (artifact hash: sha256:ab34f9...); routing layer will disable automated fallback for the route used by Veridian.
- Security controls: CMK-backed encryption (customer-provided), audit logs retained for 12 months, VPC/private networking, and attestation that routing will not be changed without 30 days’ notice.
- Availability: we will provision burst capacity and an EU AZ hot standby. Disallowing fallback means short failures will return 503 until capacity is available; we will document escalation/playbook.

Attachments: veridian_map_v1.pdf (mutual action plan), eu_data_residency_checklist.xlsx, kms_integration_notes.md

Ask: please review the MAP and the attestation. If acceptable, sign the MAP (DocuSign link included in email) and confirm a preferred pilot start date in Q4. Once signed, we’ll schedule a provisioning window (2–4 business weeks) and assign a dedicated Solutions engineer.

If Legal or Procurement would like us to change any attestation language we can iterate, but the operational constraints (no-fallback inside EU) will remain a gating factor.

Best — Mark
